name: F5 WAF — Authentication/Authorization Attack Reaching Internet Banking
description:
Attacker objective
Bypass or brute-force authentication/authorization on the internet-banking login to take over customer accounts.

Attack logic
The WAF classifies authentication/authorization attacks. A source generating many such attacks against the banking login in a short window is running a credential or authorization attack.

Why this detection works
Source aggregation over the auth/authz attack type isolates the actor; correlating with backend authentication-failure logs confirms success.

False positives
A misbehaving legitimate integration hitting auth endpoints; a scanner.

Tuning
Set the event count to local volume; correlate with backend authentication logs.

Required telemetry
F5 ASM / Advanced WAF events (CEF): attack_type (Authentication/Authorization), deviceAction, source.ip.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Review the targeted auth endpoints and whether the source also succeeded (backend logon logs).
2. A credential attack on the banking login is high priority; consider blocking.
false_positives: A misbehaving legitimate integration hitting auth endpoints; a scanner.
query: observer.vendor:"F5" and cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4:"Authentication/Authorization Attacks" and cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2 >= 4 and not cef.extensions.deviceAction:"blocked"

name: F5 WAF — Critical Attack Reached a Banking Application (SQLi/RFI/Smuggling/Malware)
description:
Attacker objective
Directly exploit an internet-banking application via a high-severity injection — SQL injection (data theft / authentication bypass), HTTP request smuggling (cache poisoning / control bypass), or remote file inclusion (RCE).

Attack logic
The WAF assigns each request an attack type and a violation rating and records whether it was blocked. A high-rating SQLi / request-smuggling / RFI / malware request that the WAF did not block reached the application backend.

Why this detection works
Scoping to high-confidence attack types with a high violation rating and a non-blocking WAF action isolates critical attacks that actually reached the app from lower-confidence signature noise.

False positives
An authorised scanner/pentest, or a WAF signature false-positive on a benign request.

Tuning
Allowlist sanctioned scanner source IPs; review the full request to confirm the injection; place the WAF policy in blocking mode to stop these outright.

Required telemetry
F5 ASM / Advanced WAF events (CEF): attack_type, violation_rating, deviceAction, source.ip, url, full request.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Review the full request and URL to confirm the injection is real (not a signature FP).
2. source.ip + target app: if confirmed, treat as active exploitation of internet banking and escalate.
3. Correlate the source with the campaign/RCE rules.
false_positives: An authorised scanner/pentest, or a WAF signature false-positive on a benign request.
query: observer.vendor:"F5" and cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4:("SQL-Injection" or "HTTP Request Smuggling Attack" or "Remote File Include" or "Trojan/Backdoor/Spyware") and cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2 >= 4 and not cef.extensions.deviceAction:"blocked"

name: F5 WAF — Critical Attack Type Passed the WAF (Single Event)
description: Single-event promotion for the highest-fidelity case: violation rating >= 4 AND attack type in (Command Execution, SQL-Injection, Remote File Include, Server Side Code Injection, Trojan/Backdoor/Spyware) AND the request was NOT blocked. Low volume, high confidence: each alert is a likely exploit reaching a banking app.
author: JCB Detection Engineering
query: observer.vendor:"F5" and cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4:("Command Execution" or "SQL-Injection" or "Remote File Include" or "Server Side Code Injection" or "Trojan/Backdoor/Spyware" or "Other Application Attacks") and cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2 >= 4 and not cef.extensions.deviceAction:"blocked"

name: F5 WAF — Scanner / Reconnaissance Burst Against Banking Applications
description: ≥30 recon-type violations (Vulnerability Scan, Forceful Browsing, Predictable Resource Location, Non-browser Client, Information Leakage) from one source in 30 minutes, any action. Catches the scanning phase the QA - F5WAF rule saw only piecemeal.
author: JCB Detection Engineering
query: observer.vendor:"F5" and cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4:("Vulnerability Scan" or "Forceful Browsing" or "Predictable Resource Location" or "Non-browser Client" or "Information Leakage")

name: F5 WAF — Single Source Attacking Multiple Banking Applications
description:
Attacker objective
Deliberately target the institution across its estate by attacking multiple distinct banking applications rather than a single opportunistic endpoint.

Attack logic
A single source attacking two or more distinct WAF-protected banking applications with high-confidence attacks indicates focused targeting of the bank rather than opportunistic scanning of one app.

Why this detection works
Counting distinct targeted applications (WAF policies) per source surfaces focused, multi-application targeting.

False positives
Shared NAT/proxy egress; authorised scanners.

Tuning
Raise the distinct-application threshold for higher confidence; allowlist known scanners.

Required telemetry
F5 ASM / Advanced WAF events (CEF): source.ip, WAF policy / application name.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Identify which banking applications were targeted and whether attacks were blocked or alerted.
2. Multi-application targeting is deliberate; prioritise and consider blocking the source.
query: observer.vendor:"F5" and cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4:("SQL-Injection" or "Cross Site Scripting (XSS)" or "Command Execution" or "Server Side Code Injection" or "Path Traversal" or "Remote File Include" or "HTTP Request Smuggling Attack" or "Detection Evasion" or "Injection Attempt" or "Authentication/Authorization Attacks" or "Trojan/Backdoor/Spyware") and cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2 >= 4

name: F5 WAF — Sustained Blocked Attack Campaign Against Banking Applications
description: ≥300 BLOCKED rating≥4 attack events from one source in ~30m — an active exploitation campaign the WAF is absorbing. Complements the not-blocked rules: today 152.70.180.122 fires 205k blocked r≥4 hits/week and no rule reports it. Suppression 6h keeps a persistent campaign to ~4 alerts/day.
author: JCB Detection Engineering
query: observer.vendor:"F5" and cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2 >= 4 and cef.extensions.deviceAction:"blocked" and cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4:* and not cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4:"N/A"

name: F5 WAF — Sustained RCE Campaign Reaching a Banking App (Code Injection / Command Execution)
description:
Attacker objective
Achieve remote code execution on the banking application backend via server-side code injection, OS command execution, or remote file inclusion.

Attack logic
RCE-class attack types are among the most dangerous a WAF classifies. A single source that lands several high-confidence RCE-class attacks the WAF did not block indicates sustained exploitation reaching the backend.

Why this detection works
When the WAF is in alert-only mode, source-based aggregation isolates a real actor from scattered signature noise; scoping to RCE-class types and a non-blocking action keeps signal high.

False positives
A scanner operating against an alert-only policy; a WAF signature false-positive on benign content.

Tuning
Adjust the event count to local volume; place the WAF policy in blocking mode to actually stop the attacks.

Required telemetry
F5 ASM / Advanced WAF events (CEF): attack_type, violation_rating, deviceAction, source.ip, full request.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Review the full request for the RCE payloads and whether any returned a 2xx response.
2. Treat as active exploitation of internet banking; escalate and consider blocking the source.
false_positives: A scanner operating against an alert-only policy; a WAF signature false-positive on benign content.
query: observer.vendor:"F5" and cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4:("Server Side Code Injection" or "Command Execution") and cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2 >= 4 and not cef.extensions.deviceAction:"blocked"

name: F5 WAF — Sustained Web Exploitation Bypassing the WAF (Single Source)
description:
Attacker objective
Successfully deliver web attacks to the internet-banking applications while the WAF is in a transparent/alert mode, so high-confidence attacks reach the backend.

Attack logic
A single source that lands many high-confidence (high violation-rating) dangerous attacks the WAF did not block within the window is repeatedly reaching a banking application.

Why this detection works
Combining a high violation rating with a non-blocking WAF action and per-source aggregation isolates an attacker reaching the backend.

False positives
An authorised scanner operating against an alert-only policy.

Tuning
Adjust the count threshold to local volume; the durable remediation is to place the WAF policy in blocking mode.

Required telemetry
F5 ASM / Advanced WAF events (CEF): attack_type, violation_rating, deviceAction, source.ip.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. source.ip landed many high-rating attacks that were not blocked, so they reached the banking backend.
2. Review the target app and attack types; assess exposure and enable WAF blocking mode.
false_positives: An authorised scanner operating against an alert-only policy.
query: observer.vendor:"F5" and cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4:("SQL-Injection" or "Cross Site Scripting (XSS)" or "Command Execution" or "Server Side Code Injection" or "Path Traversal" or "Remote File Include" or "HTTP Request Smuggling Attack" or "Session Hijacking" or "Detection Evasion" or "Trojan/Backdoor/Spyware" or "JSON Parser Attack" or "XML Parser Attack" or "Injection Attempt" or "Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)" or "HTTP Parser Attack" or "Buffer Overflow" or "HTTP Response Splitting" or "Other Application Attacks") and cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2 >= 4 and not cef.extensions.deviceAction:"blocked"

name: F5 WAF — Targeted Web-Attack Campaign Against Internet Banking
description:
Attacker objective
Compromise internet-banking applications by probing them with a broad exploitation toolkit (SQLi, XSS, command execution, code injection, traversal, RFI, request smuggling, WAF evasion).

Attack logic
A legitimate client triggers at most one or two WAF attack categories incidentally. A single source that triggers several distinct dangerous categories within a short window is running an automated or targeted web-attack toolkit against the bank.

Why this detection works
Counting distinct dangerous attack types per source separates toolkit/campaign behaviour from incidental single-category hits.

False positives
Authorised vulnerability scanners / pentests; aggressive DAST from a partner.

Tuning
Raise the distinct-type threshold or shorten the window if noisy; allowlist sanctioned scanner IPs.

Required telemetry
F5 ASM / Advanced WAF events (CEF): attack_type, source.ip, policy/app, deviceAction.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. source.ip = the attacker; review the distinct attack types and whether any were not blocked (reached the app).
2. Correlate with the targeted policy/app and block the source if hostile.
false_positives: Authorised vulnerability scanners / pentests; aggressive DAST from a partner.
query: observer.vendor:"F5" and cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4:("SQL-Injection" or "Cross Site Scripting (XSS)" or "Command Execution" or "Server Side Code Injection" or "Path Traversal" or "Remote File Include" or "HTTP Request Smuggling Attack" or "Session Hijacking" or "Detection Evasion" or "Trojan/Backdoor/Spyware" or "JSON Parser Attack" or "Injection Attempt")

name: F5 WAF — Telemetry Stopped (Log Absence)
description: Fires when NO F5 WAF events arrive in 15 minutes — the correct replacement for F5-WAF Connectivity Monitor, which alerted every minute that logs EXISTED (8.5k noise alerts). Suppression: 2h so an outage pages once.
author: JCB Detection Engineering
query: FROM logs-cef.log-* METADATA _id, _index, _version | WHERE observer.vendor == "F5" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 15 minutes | STATS f5_events = COUNT() | WHERE f5_events == 0

name: F5 WAF — Web Vulnerability Scanning / Reconnaissance
description:
Attacker objective
Map the bank's internet-facing attack surface and find exploitable endpoints before targeting.

Attack logic
A single source probing many distinct URLs with WAF-flagged attacks in a short window is running an automated vulnerability scanner. Legitimate users request only a handful of URLs.

Why this detection works
Counting distinct attacked URLs per source separates automated scanning from normal browsing.

False positives
Authorised scanners/pentests; aggressive crawlers.

Tuning
Allowlist sanctioned scanner IPs; raise the URL cardinality if noisy.

Required telemetry
F5 ASM / Advanced WAF events (CEF): source.ip, url, attack_type.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Review the distinct URLs probed and whether follow-on targeted exploitation occurred.
2. Correlate the source with the campaign/exploitation rules; block if hostile.
query: observer.vendor:"F5" and cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4:("SQL-Injection" or "Cross Site Scripting (XSS)" or "Command Execution" or "Server Side Code Injection" or "Path Traversal" or "Remote File Include" or "HTTP Request Smuggling Attack" or "Detection Evasion" or "Injection Attempt" or "Authentication/Authorization Attacks" or "Trojan/Backdoor/Spyware") and cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber2 >= 4
